clue.text: Determined to work, assembling boat

parts.note: 'I shall' expresses determination to do something
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to get busy putting a boat together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' reads as building the boat but is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open rowing or sailing vessel.

clue.text: Sandworms chopped up by person with a blade

indicators.note: worms chopped up are cut into pieces, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Worms in the sand are hacked to bits by someone wielding a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges the nine letters of SANDWORMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer or duellist is someone skilled with a sword, which is a blade.

clue.text: It's so obvious — exercise, to make us trim!

indicators.note: putting the words through some exercise works them about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fitness enthusiast insists that working out is the plain way to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' rearranges the letters of US TRIM; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement so self-evident it hardly needs saying is a platitude.

clue.text: Why, we hear, nymphs love dancing to music

indicators.note: nymphs dancing move about, so their letters, with O, are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: says the word before it is to be taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why nymphs love to dance to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges NYMPHS plus O into SYMPHON; 'we hear' turns WHY into the letter Y, which completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an extended orchestral composition.

clue.text: Leathery joints?

parts.note: joints of meat that seem made of leather, as if the horse-rider's leather seats were cuts from a sheep

explanation.walkthrough: A saddle of mutton is a cut of meat; the joke is that horse saddles are made of leather, hence 'leathery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is a joint comprising both loins of a sheep, and leather saddles suit the pun.

clue.text: Checks out on lizards

definitions.meaning: to check out is to watch over or keep under observation
large tropical lizards of the genus Varanus, such as the Komodo dragon

explanation.surface: Someone inspects lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep watch on something is to observe it, and the monitor family includes large carnivorous lizards.

clue.text: Eleven bushels of grain for the pigeon

definitions.meaning: an ancient Hebrew dry measure of roughly that quantity
a bird trained to fly back to its loft

explanation.surface: A large quantity of grain is set aside to feed a pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew measure called a homer held about eleven bushels, and a homing pigeon is called by the same word.

clue.text: Powerless, _ seemingly, yet powerful

definitions.meaning: unable to do something, read as two words, a negative plus capable

explanation.surface: Someone appears weak but in fact wields great influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ABLE the word seems to mean powerless, yet as one word it means distinguished and influential; 'seemingly' marks the split reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable person is prominent and important, while being unable is a lack of capability.

clue.text: Rain gauge

definitions.meaning: something that shows a reading, as a meter or indicator does

explanation.surface: An instrument for measuring rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A short spell of rainfall has this name, and a gauge is a device that displays a measurement.

clue.text: Gets many tied in knots, so handle it with caution!

indicators.note: something tied in knots is twisted up, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that anything with many knotted ties needs careful handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' rearranges MANY TIED; 'Gets' and 'so' are links, and the definition describes the explosive by how it must be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosives such as this nitroglycerine compound must always be treated with great care.

clue.text: Spin drierful to be agitated

indicators.note: a spin cycle tumbles things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tumble drier loaded to the brim is shaken about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drierful' is a made-up word, as much as a drier holds; 'Spin' rearranges its letters, and 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flustered and in a fluster of nervous excitement is being agitated.

clue.text: Beats the robbers wickedly taking away beer

indicators.note: the robbers' letters are treated badly and so jumbled together
the letters of the word beer are removed from the jumbled pool of letters

explanation.surface: The robbers behaving wickedly are seen to steal some beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' rearranges THE ROBBERS, and 'taking away' removes the letters B, E, E, R from that pool, leaving the six of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that pulses rhythmically beats or pounds.

clue.text: Cold on the river for the starter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
taken as written
the Somme is the river in northern France famous from the First World War

explanation.surface: A soldier recalls a cold stint on the Somme before the action starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' is a link; the definition is a menu course.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear soup is typically served as the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Used very badly then overlooked

indicators.note: something treated badly is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was mistreated and then ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges USED VERY; 'then' is a link. 'overlooked' means looked over, not ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over a landscape from above is to view or inspect it broadly.

clue.text: A vacuum or the way to find that Scottish monster

definitions.meaning: a void, a state of containing nothing

definitions.text: the way to find that Scottish monster
definitions.meaning: drain Loch Ness and whatever lives in it would be exposed

explanation.surface: Hunting the Loch Ness Monster comes down to nothing, unless you drain the loch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt with a Y for the pun: EMPTY NESS, draining Loch Ness, the Scottish lake said to hold a monster. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A void is a state of holding nothing, and draining the lake would reveal what lurks in it.

clue.text: Regretting editing erotic books

indicators.note: an editor cuts and reorders material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, the books of the Christian Bible's second part

explanation.surface: An editor feels sorry about working on racy literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'editing' rearranges EROTIC together with NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse for a wrong one has done is being penitent.

clue.text: Sportsman, in short, reaching a deadlock

definitions.meaning: the rugby fly-half is the ... half, shortened
a stalemate in which neither side gives way

explanation.surface: An athlete arrives at an impasse.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the fly-half is also called the stand-off half, here clipped. 'reaching' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby half-back position shares its name with a stalemate between opposing parties.

clue.text: Beefy winning team

parts.note: the leading team is top
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A strong, muscular team takes the honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beefy' stands for something of beef: topside is a lean cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a joint of beef cut from the upper thigh.

clue.text: Starts eating fish in my official residency

indicators.note: the start of the word eating supplies its first letter
the fish word is placed inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written
the bass is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone begins tucking into fish at their official home.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official residence and offices abroad form the diplomatic mission.

clue.text: In the interval, set me against myself

parts.note: taken as written
anti means opposed to
me is the first person pronoun, standing for oneself

explanation.surface: Someone, during a break, is torn in two minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile, during the intervening period, is a synonym of the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Invalidate enclosed article for publication

indicators.note: the article is shut inside the word for invalidate

parts.note: to annul is to declare void
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor cancels a piece submitted for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook issued once every year is a type of publication.

clue.text: Scotch tenor?

definitions.meaning: the general sense or prevailing mood of something

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Scottish singer is a tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled drink, and the essential mood of something is its prevailing tone.

clue.text: Cook needs the right oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, found in Kent

explanation.surface: A chef demands the correct oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'the' are links; an oast house is a kiln building for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat in an oven with dry heat is to bake it in fat.

clue.text: Was with the group of players returning by cutter

indicators.note: both pieces are read backwards as they come back

parts.note: taken as written
a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: Someone came back with the band on a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the whole run WAS + NONET; 'with' and 'by' are links, and the cutter is a tool, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fine-toothed handsaw for joinery is a cutting tool.

clue.text: Great novelist gets time — having become one?

parts.note: big means large or great
Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

explanation.surface: A famous novelist is sent to prison, perhaps for marrying twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets time' suggests a prison sentence; the definition is cryptic: someone who has married, become one with a spouse, more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage makes a couple one; someone who weds again while still married is a polygamist.

clue.text: Judge number of beasts, on first sighting

parts.note: asses are beasts of burden, several of them

indicators.note: the first letter of the word sighting is taken

explanation.surface: Someone estimates the size of a herd at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise is to judge.

clue.text: Agreed to enter butchery in Scotland not long ago

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

indicators.note: the letters are butchered, hacked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A butcher in Scotland recently agreed to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butchery' rearranges ENTER into TREEN; 'to' is a link. Yestreen is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for yesterday evening, meaning recently.
